title: A Plea for God to Come Down
summary_text: The prayer begs God to tear open heaven and come down, making mountains and nations tremble as He did before. The speakers confess that they have sinned, become unclean, and been swept away by their iniquities, with even their righteous acts compared to filthy rags. They call the LORD their Father and potter and ask Him not to remain angry or remember their iniquity forever. With the holy cities deserted and their beautiful temple burned, they ask whether He will keep silent and continue their suffering.

title: God Separates Rebels From His Blessed Servants
summary_text: The LORD says He made Himself known, yet His people kept provoking Him with forbidden sacrifices and practices while claiming superior holiness. He will repay their iniquities but spare His servants, whose chosen descendants will possess His mountains. Those who abandon Him for Fortune and Destiny face death, hunger, and shame, while His servants receive food, joy, and a new name. God promises to make new heavens, a new earth, and a joyful Jerusalem where weeping ceases, people live long, and families enjoy their homes and harvests. He will answer before they call, and animals will live without harming anything on His holy mountain.
key_points: God confronts rebellious worship, sacrifices in gardens, and claims of superiority, promising repayment for the people's and their fathers' iniquities.
God will preserve His servants and give His chosen heirs the mountains and pasturelands.
Those who forsake the LORD for Fortune and Destiny face death and deprivation, while His servants rejoice.
God will create new heavens and a new earth, making Jerusalem joyful and giving its people long lives.

title: Comfort for Jerusalem and Judgment for Rebels
summary_text: The LORD favors people humble in spirit who tremble at His word, while rejecting sacrifices from those who choose evil. He promises shame for their persecutors and pictures Zion giving birth suddenly, followed by motherly comfort, peace, and wealth for Jerusalem. His servants will flourish, but His wrath brings judgment by fire and sword against His enemies. God will gather nations to see His glory, send survivors to announce it, and bring His people's brothers to His holy mountain, choosing some as priests and Levites. As the new creation endures, all humanity will worship each New Moon and Sabbath and see rebels' corpses with undying worms and unending fire.
